item.title: Wall St Heads for Weekly Losses as Tech Jitters Offset Inflation Relief
item.description: U.S. stocks rose on signs of cooling inflation but a tech-led selloff—fueled by AI disruption fears—capped gains and left major indexes on track for their worst weekly losses since November.

item.title: US Consumer Prices Increase Marginally, but Inflation Pressures Persist
item.description: U.S. consumer prices rose slightly in January as cheaper gasoline and moderating rent gains were offset by higher costs for services, signaling persistent inflationary pressure that likely delays Fed rate cuts before summer.

item.title: It Wouldn’t Be Valentine’s Day Without Chocolate, No Matter the Cost
item.description: Despite elevated prices from supply-chain pressures and a 2025 price spike, Americans overwhelmingly plan to indulge in chocolate this Valentine's Day—92% hope to receive it and many will buy it for themselves—because they see it as an affordable, iconic expression of love and connection.

item.title: Why the Guthrie Kidnapping Is a Brutal Wake-up Call for Seniors Aging in Place
item.description: The terrifying disappearance of Savannah Guthrie's mother is forcing a hard look at the harsh realities of aging alone.

item.title: Airlines, Travel Groups Warn of Impact of Partial Government Shutdown on Airport Screeners
item.description: Major airlines and travel groups on Friday urged Congress to avoid a partial government shutdown, which would result in about 50,000 airport security officers not getting paid.

item.title: How the Year of the Fire Horse Can Spur You to Build Wealth in 2026
item.description: Whether you follow astrology or not, the Fire Horse can be a compelling metaphor for taking the reins of your finances.

item.title: A DHS Shutdown Is Coming. Why Travelers Should Brace for Impact.
item.description: A political impasse in Congress has pushed the Department of Homeland Security toward a partial shutdown that could disrupt TSA operations, delay pay for roughly 61,000 airport employees, hinder FEMA disaster reimbursements and affect travelers, boaters and DHS workers until lawmakers reach an agreement.
